notes: Articles appear when the learner repeats a memorized chunk ('a meeting', 'a report'), but disappear with new or compound nouns ('project architecture meeting', 'action plan').
The learner often speaks in fragments and adds the time word in a separate breath ('I had a project meeting.' + 'yesterday.'); joining it into one sentence helps both word order and articles.
'an' is pronounced as 'a', so the -n disappears before vowel-initial nouns; words like an hour, an egg, an email give it repeated chances.
Self-repair is good — after feedback the learner retries and usually fixes it within two attempts.
